Articles were considered for the meta-­analysis if they
met the following inclusion criteria: (1) they investigated
the prevalence of hypertensive emergencies in patients

or hospitalization and in-­hospital mortality due to hypertensive emergency; and (3) they were published in
English. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate a pattern of hypertension-­mediated organ damage primarily affecting the brain and
heart, substantial cardiovascular renal morbidity and mortality, as well as subsequent hospitalization in patients with hypertensive emergencies presenting to the ED.

hypertensive emergencies in other departments were excluded. The extracted data were arcsine transformed and pooled
using a random-­effects model. Fifteen studies (n=4370 patients) were included. Pooled analysis demonstrates that the prevalence of hypertensive emergencies was 0.5% (95% CI, 0.40%–­0.70%) in all patients presenting to ED and 35.9% (95% CI,
26.7%–­45.5%) among patients presenting in ED with hypertensive crisis. Ischemic stroke (28.1% [95% CI, 18.7%–­38.6%])
